chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Amr ibn Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Goodness is tied to the forelocks of the horses until the Day of Judgment.'

key_terms.بِنَوَاصِی: To the forelocks (front of the neck)

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet mean when he says goodness is tied to the forelocks of horses?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith in *Thawab al-Amal*, emphasizing the enduring virtue of horse care from the Prophet’s time through the era of the Imams. The phrase 'goodness is tied to the forelocks of horses' underscores the strategic and spiritual importance of cavalry in early Islamic expansion, linking physical preparation for jihad with divine reward. This tradition reflects the Shia scholarly view that maintaining readiness for defense is an act of worship, reinforcing the practical application of faith in societal stability.
